first_impression.reaction: Two paragraphs before the takeaways is a bit much on a phone, but the first paragraph actually lists the sequence (matchmakers, hands, wreath, loaf, game at the door, blessing, church, songs), so I got the gist straight away. The Key takeaways box is right there after it, so I stayed.

journey.quote: They are a sequence: a visit from the matchmakers, a joining of hands, a wreath, a loaf, a game at the door, a blessing, a church rite, then a long evening of song.
journey.reaction: Good, that's basically the answer in one line. Saved me scrolling.

journey.quote: The korovai, a decorated wedding bread, was traditionally baked with song, used to bless the couple and shared with every guest.
journey.reaction: Clear and specific. This is the kind of bit I'd screenshot.

journey.quote: Smartraveller advises Australians not to travel to Ukraine (as at November 2026), so these customs are best brought to a wedding in Australia or another destination.
journey.reaction: I'm not Australian and I wasn't planning to go to Ukraine, I just wanted to know the traditions. Feels like it's eating one of four takeaway slots. Nice that it's dated though.

journey.quote: The traditional Ukrainian wedding was a staged sequence of acts, from matchmaking and betrothal to the sharing of the korovai, with many regional variations.
journey.reaction: The takeaways only really name the korovai. Things like the rushnyk, the vinok and the bride ransom are what I'd want to see listed up top so I know which section to jump to.

journey.quote: This is a story told in many families rather than a rite the encyclopaedia records, and its meaning shifts with the teller.
journey.reaction: Honestly I like that they tell me what's folklore and what's documented. Most listicles just state it all as fact.

journey.quote: It is often told that the couple are crowned during the service, with crowns held above or placed on their heads, a moment shared with other Eastern rites.
journey.reaction: By now I've seen 'it is often told' a lot. I get why, but it starts to feel like the page isn't sure of anything. Skimming, I can't always tell which bits are solid.

journey.quote: It is often told that many Ukrainian couples wear the wedding ring on the right hand.
journey.reaction: That's exactly the type of quick question I'd Google. Useful FAQ, short answers.

journey.quote: No single gift is recorded as traditional in the sources we used.
journey.reaction: Bit of a non-answer if I'm a guest trying to figure out what to bring, but at least it's honest.

unanswered_questions: As a guest, is cash in an envelope normal or not? The page won't say.
Which of these traditions actually happen at most Ukrainian weddings today, versus only at very traditional ones?
Roughly how long does a modern Ukrainian wedding reception run?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Ukrainian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly clickbaity title. I typed a plain question, the heading should just say 'Ukrainian wedding traditions'.

turn_offs_found.quote: This guide walks through those customs in the order they traditionally unfold, separates what the encyclopaedia records from what families often tell, and shows how Ukrainian-Australian and mixed-heritage couples carry them into a wedding in Australia or elsewhere.
turn_offs_found.why: Second intro paragraph is describing the article instead of answering. On a train I'd skip it.

would_share_with: A friend going to a Ukrainian friend's wedding as a guest

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, a Wedded Advisor from Wedded Concierge can talk through how those moments fit the celebration you have in mind, as your single point of contact from the first conversation onwards.
cta_reaction.why: I'm not planning a wedding, I was just curious. The CTA is calm and not pushy, which I appreciate, but it's not for me right now. I might bookmark the site though.

top_3_changes: Put the named traditions (rushnyk, korovai, vinok, vykup, blessing, crowning) as a quick list in the Key takeaways so a skimmer can jump straight to one.
Swap the Smartraveller takeaway for a tradition-focused point and leave travel advice in its own section further down.
Make the title plain and drop or shorten the second intro paragraph so the takeaways sit within the first 100 words.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on her phone
No invented brand facts; missing info listed under unanswered_questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
No prices and deferred business details not treated as must-fix

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10) and not a buyer, so the low likelihood_to_enquire reflects search intent rather than a draft flaw.

assumptions: Read in fast mode: skimmed intro, Key takeaways, one or two sections and the FAQ, as the persona's decision behaviour describes.
Page load speed and pop-ups can't be judged from a markdown draft.
